title: From Agent Behaviour to Agent-Friendly Documentation: An Empirical Study of How Coding Agents Discover, Read, and Write Technical Documentation
abstract: arXiv:2608.20195v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Technical documentation is written for human developers, but an increasing share of software changes is now authored by autonomous coding agents. Which documents they consult, when, and what follows remain unknown. We conduct a behaviour-grounded study of agent-documentation interaction across two public datasets: 557 agentic coding sessions from SWE-chat, yielding 94,813 development events including 3,033 documentation interactions; and 33,097 agentic pull requests from AIDev, with 690,260 classified file-level change records. Four findings challenge current documentation practice. First, agents' documentation work is dominated by agent-facing artefacts: instruction files and working notes account for 60.5% of all documentation interactions, versus 10.6% for classical technical documentation and 1.3% for API references. Second, the link between consultation and code editing is unresolved: the adjacent transition probability is 0.002 a

translated_title: 从智能体行为到智能体友好的文档：关于编码智能体如何发现、阅读和撰写技术文档的实证研究
translated_abstract: 技术文档是为人类开发者编写的，但现在越来越多的软件变更由自主编码智能体完成。它们查阅哪些文档、何时查阅以及随后发生什么，目前仍不清楚。我们对两个公共数据集中的智能体-文档交互进行了基于行为的实证研究：来自SWE-chat的557个智能体编码会话，产生了94,813个开发事件，包括3,033次文档交互；以及来自AIDev的33,097个智能体拉取请求，包含690,260条分类的文件级变更记录。四项发现挑战了当前的文档实践。首先，智能体的文档工作主要由面向智能体的工件主导：指令文件和工作笔记占所有文档交互的60.5%，而经典技术文档仅占10.6%，API参考仅占1.3%。其次，文档查阅与代码编辑之间的联系尚未解决：相邻转换概率仅为0.002。
tldr: 本研究通过实证发现，编码智能体的文档使用主要集中于指令文件和工作笔记等面向智能体的工件，而非传统技术文档，且文档查阅与代码编辑之间的关联极弱，这挑战了现有文档实践，提示需要设计更智能体友好的文档。
en_tdlr: This empirical study reveals that coding agents predominantly interact with agent-facing artifacts like instruction files and working notes rather than traditional technical documentation, and the link between documentation consultation and code editing is extremely weak, challenging current documentation practices and calling for agent-friendly documentation design.
